**Job Description**
We have an opening for a
**Physics-Informed Machine Learning Postdoctoral Researcher**
to develop and apply advanced computational methods for modeling complex physical systems.
  
  
You will combine expertise in machine learning, computational mechanics, and numerical methods to develop physics-informed models that improve the accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency of scientific simulations. Research may include developing machine-learning models constrained by physical laws, learning constitutive relationships from experimental or simulation data, developing surrogate and reduced-order models, and integrating data-driven approaches into computational mechanics workflows. This position is in the Atmospheric, Earth and Energy Division within the Physical and Life Sciences Directorate.
  
  
*This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You will have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week.*
**You will**

* Develop physics-informed machine-learning methods for computational mechanics and scientific simulation.
* Integrate governing equations, conservation laws, boundary conditions, and material constraints into machine-learning models.
* Develop, train, validate, and evaluate neural networks, surrogate models, reduced-order models, and other scientific machine-learning methods.
* Analyze computational and experimental data to identify physical relationships, model parameters, and constitutive behavior.
* Perform computational mechanics simulations using finite-element, finite-volume, or related numerical methods.
* Pursue independent (but complementary) research interests and interact with a broad spectrum of scientists internally and externally to the Laboratory.
* Collaborate with others in a multidisciplinary team environment to accomplish research goals.
* Publish research results in peer-reviewed scientific or technical journals and present results at external conferences seminars and/or technical meetings.
* Perform other duties as assigned

**Qualifications**

* Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship.
* PhD in computational mechanics, mechanical engineering, applied mathematics, computational science, physics, materials science, or a related field.
* Demonstrated experience with physics-informed machine learning, scientific machine learning, or related data-driven modeling approaches.
* Knowledge of computational solid and/or fluid mechanics, numerical methods, and contact mechanics for Lagrangian finite element methods.
* Experience with computational simulations and analysis of scientific or engineering data. Experience with high-performance computing environments.
* Ability to develop independent research projects, including publication of peer-reviewed literature, and to communicate technical information effectively.
* Ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team environment.
* Proficient verbal and written communication skills to collaborate effectively in a team environment and present and explain technical information.

**Qualifications We Desire**

* Experience with physics-informed neural networks, neural operators, differentiable programming, or hybrid physics-based and data-driven models.
* Experience with deep learning, transfer learning, generative models, surrogate modeling, or reduced-order modeling.
* Experience with finite-element methods, computational fluid dynamics, solid mechanics, multiphysics simulation, or related computational frameworks.
* Experience with Python and machine-learning frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX or TensorFlow.

As a Behavioral Health nurse, you’ll be at the forefront of improving mental health care, helping patients find stability and hope within the community you serve. As a Resident I Mental Health Nurse, you’ll care for patients with a range of mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and co-occurring medical issues—including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression, and anxiety. You’ll build skills in de-escalation, trauma-informed care, therapeutic communication, and safe psychotropic medication administration, while working closely with psychiatrists, providers, therapists, social workers, and more. Because all nursing involves mental health, you’ll be well-prepared to grow within Behavioral Health or transition into other specialties as your career evolves.
  
  

* Patient Care Delivery: As a Resident I Graduate Nurse, you will implement nursing care plans under the supervision of an experienced Registered Nurse in a high-quality, empathetic, and patient-centered manner
* Documentation: Document observations, interactions and patient responses and report to your assigned RN, RN Preceptor, Clinical Nurse Coordinator or Charge Nurse
* Patient Education: You educate patients on their treatment plans, diagnoses, medications, possible side effects, follow-up measures and more
* Clinical Excellence: You will engage in evidence-based best practices that enhance the patient experience and patient outcomes, including SAFETY rounding, communication fundamentals/AIDET, Teach-Back, Narrating Care, etc
